request.spec:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,
the paste box and the quick-add bar.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,
the paste box and the quick-add bar.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now archive a sheet. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. The first one checks the archive itself and every refusal on an archived sheet; the other three check that `sheet-archived` shows "no" before archiving.

**What it does**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V42__sheet_archived.sql`, adds an `archived` flag to the sheet. Loading a sheet now returns it, and the screen shows `sheet-archived` as yes/no.
- **Archiving:** there's a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/archive`. Only a steward can archive, and only once. When it works it writes `SHEET_ARCHIVED sheet=<id> by=<user>` to the audit file. Anyone else, or a second attempt, is refused with the sheet's error. A refusal writes nothing.
- **Refusing changes:** I extended the existing filter that already blocks viewers (`RefuseViewerChanges.java`). It now also refuses every change to an archived sheet before any endpoint runs, so nothing is written and nothing is audited. That covers today, settings, rates, people, claims, the paste box and the quick-add bar, and each form shows its usual error.
- **Bulk open and bulk settle:** these skip the filter and do their own check instead. On an archived sheet they report every selected claim as refused (e.g. opened 0, refused 1), which is what their counters expect.
- **Screen:** the archive button sits next to the today form. The two share one `sheet-error` element, because two elements with that same id on screen would break the test's error check.

One choice to confirm: on an archived sheet, role changes and delegations are refused too, since the request said every change. If you want an archived sheet's roles to stay editable, those two paths would need excluding from the filter.
